issues.explanation: 'Avoid Exercise' is not clinically coherent with the rest of the profile. The threat items center on hypervigilance about nighttime intrusion and safety checking in the home, while the memory and appraisal items focus on intrusive assault memories, danger, and physical vulnerability. Exercise avoidance addresses a different symptom domain and lacks plausible linkage to the selected threat, memory, or appraisal content. In contrast, magical thinking and mirror checking fit better with maladaptive attempts to manage threat and distress.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened
issues.explanation: These two selected items are difficult to reconcile within the same profile. A strong appraisal of permanent bodily damage implies acknowledgment of serious ongoing physical consequences, whereas telling oneself the event did not really happen or was not that bad reflects minimization/denial of the trauma's reality or impact. While some ambivalence can occur clinically, this pair pulls in opposing directions strongly enough to question internal coherence in this profile.

vignette: Martha, a 78-year-old widowed African American woman and skilled potter, has been struggling with intrusive memories of an assault that occurred six months ago. She had always felt secure in her small home studio nestled among the trees, but now every creak or rustle outside made her jump. The assault took place on a cool spring evening when Martha was working late into the night, shaping and firing new pieces for an upcoming exhibition. A man broke into her studio through a window she had carelessly left unlocked. He entered while she was in the backroom glazing her latest creations. Startled by his sudden appearance, she froze in fear. The man, noticing her distress, took what he could from the showroom and fled. Despite feeling shaken and violated, Martha managed to call the police and recount the event. Since then, the memory of that night has forced its way into her mind at unexpected moments-whenever she hears a sudden noise or sees something out of place in her studio. The images are vivid and almost tangible; she can feel the same sense of terror rising within her as if it were happening again right now. These intrusive memories are especially distressing when she tries to relax during her evening routine, leading her to repeatedly check mirrors for any signs of the intruder's return and meticulously ensuring that all locks and windows are securely fastened. Martha has become increasingly vigilant about safety even in familiar settings. She wakes multiple times each night to check if everything is secure, unable to fully relax despite knowing she is safe at home. During her waking hours, she listens intently for any sounds of intrusion or disturbances, her body tense and alert as if still under threat. Her efforts to suppress these thoughts have only intensified the distress. She has come to believe that thinking about the event will overwhelm her, making it difficult to handle even basic tasks around the studio. Martha's world has become smaller and more constricted. The once peaceful act of working with clay now feels fraught with danger, causing her to put off completing new pieces for fear of being caught unawares. Over time, these behaviors have taken a toll on both her work and relationships. She has missed several deadlines for exhibitions and felt isolated from friends who worry about her well-being but don't fully understand her internal struggles. Martha's daughter had suggested that she seek help multiple times, but it wasn't until the assault was replayed in her mind during a quiet moment at church last week that she finally decided to reach out. Martha is most afraid of feeling perpetually unsafe and losing control over her life. She hopes therapy can help her regain some peace and security so that she might once again find joy in her work and connect with others without the constant fear looming over her. Her body's persistent reaction to danger, even when there is none, has made it difficult to move forward, but she is determined to take steps toward healing and reclaiming a sense of safety in her world.
